verdict: Avoid new SME refining/coal-products exposure in Begusarai; the data call is Avoid and the news flow is worse, so lend only to IOC-anchored service contractors with clean receivables, and decline all standalone processing units.
title: Begusarai Petroleum Refining & Coal Products: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is here
Begusarai's refining economy is Barauni refinery, an IOC asset, and the SME layer around it is not refining itself but the service and processing ring: road and civil contractors, tanker and logistics operators, small coke and coal-products traders, and job-work units feeding the plant [1][2][3]. **Cash is made on throughput and contracts, not on price; the SME earns a margin on service, while the crude price risk sits with IOC.** So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower sells to IOC or to the open market; if open market, ask who bears the inventory loss when Brent moves.

## Where value and cash actually sit
Value sits in the contract and the receivable, not the asset. **The working-capital cycle is the whole credit story: bill IOC, wait for payment, fund the gap.** Capex is modest for service contractors but heavy for any unit buying processing equipment. Brent at $113/bbl is above the $75–100 band [D], which inflates input cost for anyone holding feedstock and squeezes the small trader. IOC's own under-recovery on cylinders rose from INR 184 in September to INR 229 in October and is projected at INR 309 in November and INR 370 in December [6] — that is pressure on the anchor, and it flows to vendor payment timing. Collect from customer the receivable days and the IOC contract tenure.

## What has broken now
Bihar GST collections are -0.1% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, 6.2 pp slower [D], and NIC 19 output is -0.6% YoY with -0.9% Apr-to-date [D]. **The local demand signal is weak while the national output signal is also negative — this is not a Begusarai-only problem.** The local news is thin and old: two October 2026 reports are only about refinery road repair demands to IOC [1][2], and an August 2026 report is a flag-hoisting item [3]. Say plainly: sources tell us little about Begusarai credit conditions, so lean on first principles and peers. Peer results are strong — HPCL's GRM rose to US$32.2/bbl, +35% QoQ and +262% YoY [7], and BPCL beat on refining [4] — but that is refiner margin, not SME margin. Do not read peer GRM as a signal for a small contractor.

## Who to pursue and how to grow safely
Pursue IOC-anchored civil and road contractors with written work orders, tanker operators on fixed haulage contracts, and job-work units with IOC as sole buyer. Avoid standalone coal-products traders, open-market coke dealers, and any unit whose receivable is a single private counterparty. **Structure against the receivable: assign IOC dues, keep tenor inside the contract, and take monthly GST returns, IOC payment advices, and bank statements every month.** If the borrower cannot show an IOC payment advice in the last quarter, ask for the contract copy and the last three invoices before any enhancement.

## Early-warning signs
- GST turnover vs bank credits (monthly): divergence beyond 10% -> stop disbursement and re-verify invoices.
- IOC payment advice lag (monthly): receivable days stretching past contract terms -> reduce limit and seek assignment.
- Brent above $100/bbl (weekly): feedstock-holding borrower margin compression -> shift to service-only exposure.
- Bihar GST run-rate (monthly): stays negative while India positive -> cap new-to-bank SME limits.
